Fully compensated foundation: the weight of the excavated soil is greater than that of the building, and the net stress transferred to the subsoil is “negative” – with a sufficiently rigid RC raft the structure is practically immobile. (With overcompensation the soil may heave; below the water table uplift also has to be checked.)
Partly compensated: ${pct}% of the load is “counterbalanced” by the excavated soil – settlement arises only from the excess, and starts only when construction exceeds the unloading.
Weak compensation: the excavated soil counterbalances only a small part of the load. Try more basement levels!
